chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The woman who has the option (of divorce) is separated (mutlaqah) from the moment, without a formal divorce, and there is no inheritance between them, because the bond of marriage has severed from her at the time that option was exercised by her and by the husband.'

key_terms.اَلْعِصْمَةَ: The bond of marriage / the rope of marriage
key_terms.اَلْمُخَيَّرَةُ: The woman who has the right of option (khayr) in marriage
key_terms.تَبِينُ: She is separated/declared free (from the bond of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a woman who exercises her right of option (khayr) in marriage regarding divorce and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies that the exercise of the right of option (khayr) acts as an automatic, immediate severance of the marital bond (fasl) without requiring a formal divorce pronouncement (talaq). Consequently, the couple is treated as strangers regarding inheritance, as the 'bond of chastity' ('ismah) is broken at the precise moment the option is exercised. This ruling underscores the unique status of conditional clauses in Shia jurisprudence, where the condition's fulfillment directly alters legal status without procedural delay.
